subject: quantitative_aptitude
question: A and B can complete a work together in 30 days. They worked together for 20 days, and then B left. A finished the remaining work alone in another 20 days. In how many days could A alone complete the entire work from the beginning?
explanation: In 20 days, A and B together completed 20/30 = 2/3 of the total work. Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the total work. A finished this remaining 1/3 work in 20 days. Hence, A alone can complete the full work (1 whole unit) in 20 / (1/3) = 60 days.

subject: quantitative_aptitude
question: A tank has three pipes: A, B, and C. A and B can fill it in 3 hours and 4 hours respectively, while C can empty it in 1 hour. If the pipes are opened in order at 3:00 PM, 4:00 PM, and 5:00 PM on the same day, at what time will the tank become completely empty?
explanation: Assume tank capacity = LCM(3, 4, 1) = 12 units. Pipe A filling rate = +4 units/hr; Pipe B filling rate = +3 units/hr; Pipe C emptying rate = -12 units/hr. From 3 PM to 4 PM (1 hr): Only A is open => fills 4 units. From 4 PM to 5 PM (1 hr): A and B are open => fill 4 + 3 = 7 units. At 5:00 PM, total water in tank = 4 + 7 = 11 units. At 5:00 PM, pipe C opens. Net rate of all 3 pipes = 4 + 3 - 12 = -5 units/hr (net emptying of 5 units/hr). Time to empty the 11 units = 11 / 5 hours = 2 hours and 1/5 hour = 2 hours and 12 minutes. Time of full emptying = 5:00 PM + 2 hrs 12 mins = 7:12 PM.
